source.publisher: Tribunals Ontario — Landlord and Tenant Board

notes: Use the current official form version. Form versions and URLs may change.
The standard lease (2229E) is published by the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing through the Central Forms Repository, not by the Landlord and Tenant Board; the updater does not manage it.

The Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 requires the standard lease for most private residential tenancies entered into on or after April 30, 2018. Exemptions apply (care homes, mobile home parks and land lease communities, most social housing, and others); check Part A of the form's General Information.
A property manager may prepare or serve a form as an authorized agent, but the legal party remains the landlord or tenant unless the form or law states otherwise.
A form does not itself create authority to end a tenancy, increase rent, enter a unit, or recover money; the applicable legislation and required process control.

landlord_vs_property_manager.landlord: The owner or legal entity that is the landlord under the tenancy agreement. The landlord remains responsible for statutory obligations even when an agent performs administrative tasks.
landlord_vs_property_manager.property_manager_or_authorized_agent: A person or company authorized to act for the landlord. The manager may complete, sign, serve, receive, file, or respond to forms only within the authority granted by the landlord and the applicable form or process.
landlord_vs_property_manager.tenant: The person or persons named as tenant(s) under the tenancy agreement. A tenant signs tenant-originated forms and receives landlord notices.
landlord_vs_property_manager.practical_rule: Identify the legal landlord in section 1 of the standard lease and put an agent's contact details in section 3 where the form permits. Keep written proof of agency authority.

document_controls: Record the form ID, version date, completion date, service date, serving person, recipient, service method, and proof of service.
Use the official Board form rather than reproducing a private form when the Board requires a prescribed form.
Give the tenant a copy of the signed standard lease within 21 days of signing; the tenant's remedies under the Act depend on it.
Keep the signed lease, any attachment of additional terms, every notice served, proof of service, and the rent ledger together for any later application.

forms.form_name: Residential Tenancy Agreement (Standard Form of Lease)
forms.property_manager_role: May prepare the lease and be named as contact in section 3, but the landlord's legal name goes in section 1 and the landlord (or an authorized signatory) signs.
forms.use_when: Starting a private residential tenancy in Ontario on or after April 30, 2018 that is not exempt from the standard lease requirement.
do_not_use_when: The tenancy is exempt: care homes, sites in mobile home parks and land lease communities, most social and supportive housing, co-operative housing, or a tenancy where the tenant shares a kitchen or bathroom with the owner or the owner's family.
The tenancy began before April 30, 2018 and neither party has requested the standard lease.
forms.legal_effect: Sets the terms of the tenancy. Sections 1 to 17 are mandatory and cannot be changed; additional terms in an attachment cannot take away a right or responsibility under the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006.
source_basis: The catalogued PDF is the static variant (2229E 2020/12): 14 pages with AcroForm fields, fillable without XFA support. The default download on the dataset page is a dynamic XFA form that renders a single placeholder page in readers without XFA.

forms.form_name: Application about Whether the Act Applies
forms.use_when: Either party needs the Board to decide whether the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 applies to the living arrangement.
forms.legal_effect: Declaratory order that determines whether the Board has jurisdiction over the tenancy.

forms.form_name: Application about a Sublet or an Assignment
forms.use_when: The landlord seeks to evict an unauthorized occupant or overholding subtenant, or the tenant claims the landlord arbitrarily or unreasonably refused consent to assign or sublet.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order eviction of an unauthorized occupant, authorize an assignment or sublet, or end the tenancy at the tenant's request.

forms.form_name: Application to Vary the Amount of a Rent Reduction
forms.use_when: Either party wants the Board to vary an automatic rent reduction that followed a decrease in the property's municipal taxes.
forms.legal_effect: Board order sets the rent reduction amount that replaces the automatic calculation.

forms.form_name: Application to evict a tenant for non-payment of rent and to collect rent the tenant owes
forms.use_when: An N4 was served, the termination date has passed, and the rent remains unpaid.
forms.legal_effect: Asks the Board to terminate the tenancy, evict, and order payment of arrears; the tenant can still stop the eviction by paying everything owed before the order is enforced.

forms.form_name: Application to End a Tenancy and Evict a Tenant or Collect Money
forms.use_when: A notice other than N4 was served (N5, N6, N7, N8, N12, N13) and the tenant has not moved out, or the landlord relies on another ground the Act allows without notice.
forms.legal_effect: Asks the Board to terminate the tenancy and evict; may include a claim for damage, compensation for overholding, or other money.

forms.form_name: Application to End a Tenancy – Tenant Gave Notice or Agreed to Terminate the Tenancy
forms.use_when: The tenant gave an N9 or signed an N11 and did not move out by the termination date.
forms.legal_effect: Asks the Board to end the tenancy and evict without a hearing in most cases, if filed within 30 days of the termination date.

forms.form_name: Application to End a Tenancy and Evict a Tenant – Tenant Failed to Meet Conditions of a Settlement or Order
forms.use_when: The tenant breached a condition of a Board mediated settlement or order that allowed the landlord to apply without notice.
forms.legal_effect: Asks the Board to end the tenancy and evict under the terms of the earlier settlement or order.

forms.form_name: Application for a Rent Increase Above the Guideline
forms.use_when: The landlord seeks a rent increase above the guideline for eligible capital expenditures, extraordinary municipal tax or utility increases, or security services.
forms.legal_effect: Board order sets the permitted increase and its timing; the N1 must still be served, and the increase is capped at the guideline plus 3 percent per year for capital work.

forms.form_name: Application for Review of a Work Order about Provincial Maintenance Standards
forms.use_when: The landlord wants the Board to review a municipal or provincial work order issued under the provincial maintenance standards.
forms.legal_effect: The Board may confirm, vary or quash the work order.

forms.form_name: Application to Transfer a Care Home Tenant
forms.use_when: The landlord wants to transfer a care home tenant who no longer requires the level of care provided, or requires care the home does not provide.
forms.legal_effect: Board order may end the tenancy and require the tenant to move to appropriate accommodation.

forms.form_name: Application Because the Tenant Changed the Locks
forms.use_when: The tenant changed the locking system without the landlord's consent and did not provide keys.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order the tenant to provide keys, pay costs, or in some cases end the tenancy.

forms.form_name: Application to Collect Rent the Tenant Owes
forms.use_when: The landlord wants to collect rent arrears from a current tenant without ending the tenancy.
forms.legal_effect: Board order for payment of rent owed; does not affect the tenant's right to stay.

forms.form_name: Application to Collect Money a Former Tenant Owes
forms.use_when: A former tenant owes rent, compensation, utilities, or damage costs and moved out no more than one year ago.
forms.legal_effect: Board order for payment against a former tenant; before the former tenant provision, such claims went to Small Claims Court.

forms.form_name: Notice of Rent Increase
forms.use_when: Raising the rent of a unit covered by the annual rent increase guideline, at least 12 months after the tenancy began or the last increase.
do_not_use_when: The unit is exempt from the guideline (use N2).
The unit is a care home (use N3).
forms.legal_effect: Takes effect only if given at least 90 days before the increase date and the increase does not exceed the guideline unless the Board has approved more.

forms.form_name: Notice of Rent Increase (Unit Partially Exempt)
forms.use_when: Raising the rent of a unit that is exempt from the annual guideline, such as one first occupied for residential purposes after November 15, 2018.
do_not_use_when: The unit is subject to the guideline (use N1).
forms.legal_effect: Still requires 90 days' written notice and 12 months since the last increase; the guideline cap does not apply.

forms.form_name: Notice to Increase the Rent and/or Charges for Care Services and Meals
forms.use_when: Raising the rent, or the charges for care services and meals, in a care home.
forms.legal_effect: Rent portion follows the same 90-day and 12-month rules as N1; care service and meal charges follow the care home provisions of the Act.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy Early for Non-payment of Rent
forms.use_when: Rent is unpaid after the due date and the landlord wants to start the eviction process.
forms.legal_effect: Gives the tenant a termination date at least 14 days out (7 days for daily or weekly tenancies); the notice is void if the tenant pays everything owed before the termination date. A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy for Interfering with Others, Damage or Overcrowding
forms.use_when: The tenant or a guest substantially interferes with others' reasonable enjoyment or the landlord's lawful rights, causes undue damage, or overcrowds the unit.
forms.legal_effect: A first N5 gives the tenant seven days to correct the problem, which voids the notice; a second N5 within six months cannot be voided. A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy for Illegal Acts or Misrepresenting Income in a Rent-Geared-to-Income Rental Unit
forms.use_when: The tenant or a guest commits an illegal act or carries on an illegal business in the residential complex, or the tenant misrepresented income in a rent-geared-to-income unit.
forms.legal_effect: No opportunity to void; the termination period depends on the ground (10 days for illegal drug activity, otherwise 20 days). A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy for Causing Serious Problems in the Rental Unit or Residential Complex
forms.use_when: The tenant or a guest seriously impairs safety, wilfully causes undue damage, or, where the landlord lives in the same building, substantially interferes with the landlord's enjoyment.
do_not_use_when: The problem is one the tenant should be given a chance to correct (use N5).
forms.legal_effect: 10-day notice with no opportunity to void. A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy at the End of the Term
forms.use_when: Ending a tenancy at the end of its term or period for persistent late rent, the tenant no longer qualifying for subsidized housing, the unit having been provided as a condition of employment, or similar term-end grounds listed on the form.
forms.legal_effect: Requires at least 60 days' notice ending on the last day of the term or rental period (28 days for daily or weekly tenancies). A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Tenant's Notice to End the Tenancy
forms.use_when: The tenant wants to end the tenancy.
forms.legal_effect: At least 60 days' notice ending on the last day of a rental period (28 days for daily or weekly tenancies); a fixed-term tenant cannot end before the term expires except as the Act allows.

forms.form_name: Agreement to Increase the Rent Above the Guideline
forms.use_when: The landlord and tenant agree in writing to a rent increase above the guideline in exchange for capital work or a new or added service.
forms.legal_effect: Binding written agreement capped at the guideline plus 3 percent; the tenant may cancel within five days of signing, and may apply to the Board if the landlord does not deliver the work or service.

forms.form_name: Agreement to End the Tenancy
forms.use_when: The landlord and tenant both agree to end the tenancy on a chosen date.
forms.legal_effect: Binding once signed by both; a landlord cannot require it as a condition of entering the tenancy, and an agreement signed at that time is void.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy Because the Landlord, a Purchaser or a Family Member Requires the Rental Unit
forms.use_when: The landlord, a purchaser, or a specified family member or caregiver requires the unit for their own residential use for at least one year.
do_not_use_when: The landlord is a corporation (except where the purchaser is an individual).
forms.legal_effect: At least 60 days' notice ending on the last day of a rental period, plus compensation of one month's rent or an equivalent unit; bad-faith use exposes the landlord to a T5 application and administrative fines. A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Notice to End your Tenancy Because the Landlord Wants to Demolish the Rental Unit, Repair it or Convert it to Another Use
forms.use_when: The landlord intends to demolish the unit, convert it to non-residential use, or do repairs or renovations so extensive that vacant possession is required.
forms.legal_effect: At least 120 days' notice ending on the last day of a rental period; compensation and, for repairs, the tenant's right of first refusal apply. A notice of termination does not end the tenancy by itself; if the tenant does not move out the landlord must apply to the Board for an eviction order.

forms.form_name: Tenant's Notice to End my Tenancy Because of Fear of Sexual or Domestic Violence and Abuse
forms.use_when: A tenant or a child living with them is at risk of sexual or domestic violence and the tenant needs to leave early.
forms.legal_effect: Allows 28 days' notice regardless of the term, filed with the tenant statement or a court order; the landlord must keep the notice confidential.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application for a Rebate
forms.use_when: The tenant seeks a refund of money the landlord collected illegally, such as an unlawful deposit, key charge, or rent above the lawful amount.
forms.legal_effect: Board order for repayment; must generally be filed within one year of the payment.

forms.form_name: Application about Tenant Rights
forms.use_when: The landlord entered illegally, changed locks, withheld vital services, harassed or substantially interfered with the tenant, or the tenant seeks a remedy for other rights breaches.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order a rent abatement, compensation, an administrative fine, or that the landlord stop the conduct.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application for a Rent Reduction
forms.use_when: Services or facilities were reduced or removed, or the property's municipal taxes decreased, and the tenant seeks a lower rent.
forms.legal_effect: Board order reducing the lawful rent, in some cases retroactively.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application – Landlord did not Comply with an Agreement to Increase Rent Above the Guideline
forms.use_when: The landlord took an above-guideline increase under an N10 agreement but did not do the capital work or provide the service promised.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order the rent reduced to what it would have been and repayment of the excess.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application – Landlord Gave a Notice of Termination in Bad Faith
forms.use_when: The tenant moved out after an N12 or N13 and the landlord did not use the unit as stated in the notice.
forms.legal_effect: Board may award rent differential, moving costs, other compensation, and an administrative fine; must be filed within one year of moving out.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application about Maintenance
forms.use_when: The landlord has not kept the unit or complex in good repair or complied with health, safety, housing or maintenance standards.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order repairs, rent abatement, compensation, or authorize the tenant to do the work and deduct the cost.

forms.form_name: Tenant Application about Suite Meters
forms.use_when: The landlord did not comply with the suite meter rules when making the tenant responsible for electricity.
forms.legal_effect: Board may order rent abatement, compensation, or that the landlord resume providing electricity.
